Dan (AE): looping in security for a prospect RFP. They asked specifically about at-rest encryption, BYOK/HSM attestation, and rotation for Dedicated/Private.
Alice (SE): quick summary: data at rest encrypted with AES-256-GCM; in-transit uses TLS 1.3. We use envelope encryption: data encryption keys (DEKs) for blobs, encrypted by a key-encryption-key (KEK) managed in the customer's KMS/HSM when BYOK is enabled.
Eve (Customer Sec): do keys ever leave our HSM or KMS unencrypted? Need explicit vendor-safe language for our risk team. Also want FIPS level for HSMs and sample attestation docs.
Claire (Security): vendor-safe answer: "When customer-managed KMS/HSM is configured, Redwood stores only encrypted key material. Customers either import keys (HSM import) or provide wrapped keys; Redwood does not have the ability to export or retrieve unwrapped customer key material from customer-managed HSMs/KMS." We can provide CloudHSM/FIPS attestation materials under NDA.
Ben (Infra): runtime notes: KEKs remain in HSM or KMS. Short-lived DEKs are generated and used in secure process memory; DEKs are rewrapped and never persisted unencrypted. No plaintext KEKs on disk.
Eve (Customer Sec): rotation policy? We need recommended cadence and whether Redwood can automate rewraps during rotation.
Alice (SE): recommended cadence: align with customer's policy (common defaults: 90 days for CMKs, DEKs rotated per session or per-request depending on workload). For customer-managed keys Redwood will not silently rotate the CMK; rotation is either customer-driven or done via an agreed orchestration (we can assist with scripted rollover and key alias swaps). For service-managed keys (hosted API) we rotate per infra policy and provide logs.
Eve (Customer Sec): HSM specifics: which HSMs supported and certs?
Claire (Security): supported: AWS CloudHSM (FIPS 140-2 validated modules), Google Cloud HSM, Azure Dedicated HSM; on-prem customers can bring validated HSMs (nShield, Luna, etc.). We provide attestation reports and FIPS cert copies under NDA.
Dan (AE): can we package a one-paragraph RFP answer plus a one-page checklist for the security reviewer? They also requested CAIQ/SIG extracts.
Claire (Security): yes. I'll post an approved RFP paragraph and a one-page checklist in ~20m. I'll also upload CAIQ v3 + SIG Lite + SOC2 summary and the redacted HSM attestation bundle to secure storage.
infra-bot: uploaded to s3://redwood-sec/4821/risk-pack.zip
Alice (SE): sample config for Private/Dedicated (YAML) we give customers: ```kms:
  provider: aws
  mode: byok
  key_identifier: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
  import_mode: wrapped
  rotation: customer_managed
```
Ben (Infra): note for POC: we can demo BYOK import flow and live rotation with a test CloudHSM cluster. No production keys required for demo.
Eve (Customer Sec): thanks. Last ask: can you confirm whether Redwood supports client-side proof-of-possession or HSM PIN challenge during operations?
Alice (SE): for on-prem HSMs you can require PINs or access controls in your orchestration; for cloud KMS we recommend IAM + grants and we support key-grant scoped calls. Proof-of-possession for client-side encryption patterns is possible; we'll include example patterns in the checklist.
Dan (AE): great. Claire/Alice, please drop the approved paragraph and checklist into this thread and I'll attach to the RFP response.
Claire (Security): will do. :white_check_mark:
